Interface ModelMemory

public interface ModelMemory
A block of a language model's memory: the JLM1 file as it was loaded, or the attention cache. The engine reads it through int8 rows, each a little-endian float scale followed by its signed-byte values, which is how a JLM1 table stores a row and how the cache stores a key or a value. The row loops run here, next to the memory, so on the board they are the only native code of the engine.

    attend(int keyOffset, int valueOffset, int stride, int rows, int skip, int cols, float[] query, float[] scores, float divisor, float[] out)
    One attention head over the cache: rows keys from keyOffset and values from valueOffset, stride bytes apart, each using its values skip to skip + cols.
    void
    multiplyRows(int offset, int stride, int rows, int skip, int cols, float[] x, int xOffset, float[] y)
    For each of rows rows, stride bytes apart from offset, sets y[r] to the row's scale times the sum over c < cols of value skip + c times x[xOffset + c], summed in column order.
    void
    quantizeRow(int offset, float[] x, int cols)
    Writes x[0..cols) at offset as one row: the scale is the largest magnitude over 127 (at least 1e-20 / 127), and each value rounds half away from zero.

    • attend

      void attend(int keyOffset, int valueOffset, int stride, int rows, int skip, int cols, float[] query, float[] scores, float divisor, float[] out)
      One attention head over the cache: rows keys from keyOffset and values from valueOffset, stride bytes apart, each using its values skip to skip + cols. Scores each key as the dot product with query[skip..skip + cols) times its scale over divisor into scores, turns them into softmax weights (0 below -60), and writes the weighted sum of the values into out[skip..skip + cols).
